summary: A hemiparasitic shrub that grafts to host trees via modified roots (F24), stealing water and minerals while photosynthesising. The dense air (F4) and fog (F8) reduce transpiration costs, allowing it to thrive in the canopy where it uses red-purple screens (D23) against higher UV.

links: Attaches to host xylem to steal water and dissolved minerals
Shared biochemistry (F24) permits vascular grafting across lineages
Dense air (F4) and fog (F8) lower transpiration costs, making theft efficient
Host grows tall in response, concentrating the parasite in the nutrient-rich canopy
chains.play: Siphon (Control): drain vitality from a target to heal self or empower attacks. Weakness: Useless if target has high toxin resistance; effect ends if parasite is torn off.

plausibility.summary: Canopy hemiparasite with haustoria, red-purple stress pigments, and toxic fruit fits D23, F8 fog, D29 parasitic-plant niche, and alula seed dispersal. High pO₂ (F5) makes alkaloid synthesis affordable.
fixes: F24 grafting across lineages is highly speculative—in-world, frame as deep-time coevolved haustorial compatibility, not arbitrary cross-species vascular fusion. Humid dense air lowers transpiration for host and parasite, so theft pays mainly where mineral or light stress limits hosts; keep berries honestly toxic (red-vein signalling, D23).

analogues.mechanism: Haustoria tap host xylem for water and minerals while the parasite retains photosynthesis; fruits are bird-dispersed but often chemically defended (Press & Phoenix, 2005, from memory, unverified).

links: Berries concentrate host minerals and alkaloids
Red-purple pigments signal toxicity and UV stress to herbivores (D25)
High oxygen (F5) supports costly alkaloid synthesis
Birds like Alula disperse seeds via fruit (F27)
chains.play: Toxic Sap (Attack): spit corrosive sap that poisons and damages armour. Weakness: Sap dries rapidly in wind (F19); Albinos can resist the poison (Creature canon).
